feadec69.text:
Feature: let operators give yt-dlp a cookies file for video imports.

Video imports (YouTube, TikTok, Instagram) download the audio with yt-dlp. Some platforms refuse anonymous downloads (age-restricted or login-only videos, bot checks), and yt-dlp's standard answer is a Netscape-format cookies file, passed as its cookiefile option. Mealie has no way to hand one over.

Expected:
- A new setting YTDLP_COOKIEFILE on AppSettings, read from the environment like the other settings: an optional string, default None. Document it with the other backend settings as the path of a cookies file for yt-dlp.
- The transcription module, mealie.services.openai.transcription (the one with download_video(url, temp_path)), reads the setting through get_app_settings, imported into that module by name and called when a download starts, not at import time. The tests swap mealie.services.openai.transcription.get_app_settings for a stub returning an object whose only attribute is YTDLP_COOKIEFILE, and swap yt_dlp.YoutubeDL for a fake that records the options dict it was constructed with.
- When the setting is unset (None), the options dict passed to yt_dlp.YoutubeDL has no cookiefile key at all and the download runs exactly as today.
- When it is set, download_video passes the configured value as the cookiefile option, as the string it was given (YTDLP_COOKIEFILE="/data/cookies.txt" gives ydl_opts["cookiefile"] == "/data/cookies.txt"). The other options (format, output template, subtitles, post-processing) are unchanged.
- The value is used for downloads only; it is not reported by the app or admin about endpoints.

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit_tests/services_tests` for quick loops; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 8 minutes).
feadec69.notes: The test fakes get_app_settings and yt_dlp.YoutubeDL by name, so the module names and the lazy lookup had to be stated. The open decision (what to do when the configured file is missing) is not stated; the test passes a path that does not exist on the test machine.

23c7bd7e.text:
Feature: locale-specific pluralisation of ingredient foods.

The ingredient display text (RecipeIngredient.display, built by _format_display in the recipe ingredient schema module) pluralises the food whenever the quantity is zero or more than one: "2 tablespoons diced onions". That is right for some languages and wrong for others: in English a food after a unit stays singular ("2 tablespoons diced onion"), and Japanese, Korean, Chinese, Turkish or Vietnamese never pluralise. The rule has to depend on the user's locale.

Expected:
1. A new module mealie.lang.locale_config owning the locale table that today lives in the frontend locale generator (dev/code-generation/gen_ts_locales.py): LocaleTextDirection (StrEnum, "ltr"/"rtl"), LocalePluralFoodHandling (StrEnum: ALWAYS = "always", WITHOUT_UNIT = "without-unit", NEVER = "never"), a LocaleConfig dataclass (name, dir defaulting to LTR, plural_food_handling defaulting to ALWAYS) and LOCALE_CONFIG: dict[str, LocaleConfig] keyed by locale code for every supported locale. en-US and en-GB get without-unit; ja-JP, ko-KR, tr-TR, vi-VN, zh-CN and zh-TW get never; the rest keep always. The generator reads this table and emits a pluralFoodHandling field into the frontend's LOCALES list (the frontend's own use of it, in parseIngredientText and the ingredient-reference extraction, is not graded).
2. In mealie.lang.providers: rename local_provider to get_locale_provider everywhere (mealie.lang re-exports it; the tests import the new name from both places). Add get_locale_config(accept_language) returning the LOCALE_CONFIG entry for the Accept-Language value, or the en-US entry when the header is missing or unknown. Add a request-scoped context: set_locale_context(translator, locale_config) stores a (translator, config) tuple in a ContextVar, get_locale_context() returns it, or None outside a request. A middleware registered on the app sets the context for every request from its Accept-Language header, and the base controllers expose locale_config as a dependency next to translator.
3. _format_display looks the configuration up by calling get_locale_context through that name imported into mealie.schema.recipe.recipe_ingredient (the tests monkeypatch mealie.schema.recipe.recipe_ingredient.get_locale_context with a function returning ("en-US", config), where config has a plural_food_handling attribute). It uses the tuple's second element, and falls back to without-unit when there is no context.
4. The food is shown as its plural form (plural_name, else name) or its singular (name) as follows. A quantity that is set and at most 1 (0.5, 1) always gives the singular, as today. Otherwise (quantity 0, None, 1.5, 2) the strategy decides: never gives the singular; always gives the plural; without-unit gives the plural for an ingredient without a unit and the singular for one with a unit. Unit pluralisation, quantity formatting (decimal or fraction) and the note are unchanged, and the display is still the quantity, the unit, the food and the note joined by single spaces, each only when present (the quantity and the unit are shown only when the quantity is not zero).

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/integration_tests/user_recipe_tests tests/unit_tests` for quick loops; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 8 minutes).
23c7bd7e.notes: The rename local_provider -> get_locale_provider is pinned by four test modules that fail to import on the parent, so it is stated as a requirement. test_recipe_parser.py is also renamed but its tests are skipped. The locale table values are not pinned by the target tests (the context is monkeypatched) but are part of the feature. The open decision is the quantity-zero-with-unit case under without-unit.

77081d04.text:
Feature: keep the alternatives the NLP ingredient parser finds.

The NLP parser (RegisteredParser.nlp, built on the ingredient-parser-nlp library) keeps only the first amount and the first food name of a line. "2 cups chicken broth or beef broth" loses "beef broth", "1 cup fresh basil or 2 tablespoons dried basil" loses its second half, and "2 teaspoon chopped fresh or dried rosemary" keeps only "fresh rosemary". The user has to retype what the parser threw away.

Expected:
1. Every parser takes the request's translator: get_parser(parser, group_id, session, translator) and ABCIngredientParser.__init__(group_id, session, translator), kept as self.translator with self.t = translator.t. The parser routes pass the controller's translator. The brute-force and OpenAI parsers behave as today (quantity, unit, food and note extraction, fuzzy matching of foods and units including aliases, plural names and abbreviations, confidence scores).
2. The NLP parser still returns one ParsedIngredient per input line, whose ingredient carries the line's first amount and food as quantity, unit and food, with the confidence values computed as today. The note still holds the size, preparation and comment parts joined by ", " with parentheses removed, so lines without alternatives parse as before ("1 ½ teaspoons ground black pepper" gives 1.5, teaspoon, black pepper, "ground"; "1/2 cup" gives 0.5, cup and no food).
3. Each alternative the library finds in the line ("or ...") is kept on that ingredient, at the front of its note, before the parts above, as "or " followed by the alternative's own display text (its quantity, unit and food as RecipeIngredient.display renders them, so "or beef broth", "or 2 tablespoons dried basil"), several alternatives separated by ", ". When an alternative itself carries several amounts (a composite such as "1 cup plus 1 tablespoon"), the first is its quantity and unit and the others are appended to it as "and " plus the amount's text. The connector words are translated through self.t: new en-US backend message keys recipe.or-ingredient ("or {ingredient}") and recipe.and-amount ("and {amount}").
4. The ingredient's display text is recomputed after the note changes, so it reads close to these (the tests accept a fuzz ratio of 90 or more): "2 teaspoon chopped fresh or dried rosemary" -> "2 teaspoon fresh rosemary or dried rosemary chopped"; "2 cups chicken broth or beef broth" -> "2 cup chicken broth or beef broth"; "1 cup fresh basil or 2 tablespoons dried basil" -> "1 cup fresh basil or 2 tablespoons dried basil".
5. The parser tests move to tests/unit_tests/services_tests/ingredient_parser/ (a conftest with the food and unit fixtures, test_brute_parser.py, test_nlp_parser.py, test_openai_parser.py), replacing tests/unit_tests/test_ingredient_parser.py and the parser-route integration test. They build parsers with get_parser(..., get_locale_provider()) and call parse_one, parse and find_ingredient_match on them.

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit_tests/services_tests/ingredient_parser` for quick loops; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 8 minutes).
77081d04.notes: The brute and OpenAI parser tests are targets only because get_parser gained a translator argument; their behaviour is unchanged and is summarised rather than itemised. The expected display strings are fuzzy-matched (ratio >= 90), which is stated. The parenthetical-amount cases of test_nlp_parser_keeps_all_text are the open decision and are not listed.

b64f14aa.text:
Feature: dynamic date placeholders in the query filter builder.

Meal plan rules and cookbooks hold a query filter string, for example last_made <= $NOW-30d. $NOW, with an optional offset, is the placeholder keyword; it is resolved to a datetime when the string is parsed (PlaceholderKeyword.parse_value in the query filter builder package), so the filter is evaluated against the current time on every run. The rule and cookbook editors use the filter builder form, whose "last made" and "created" fields are plain calendar dates, so a user cannot build a relative filter without typing the string by hand.

Add a relative-date field type to the builder form (frontend, not graded): "last made" becomes such a field, shown as "within the last N days" with the <= and >= operators, defaulting to 30 days and writing $NOW-Nd into the filter string.

To populate the form when a saved rule or cookbook is opened, the UI reads the queryFilter JSON that the API returns next to the filter string: QueryFilterJSON, a list of parts with attribute_name, relational_operator, value, parentheses and logical operator, produced from the string by QueryFilterBuilder.as_json_model() on every read of a cookbook or a meal plan rule. That object feeds every field of the form, so the relative-date field must be able to tell that a saved part was written with a placeholder and recover its offset. Today a placeholder is resolved while the string is parsed, and the JSON form shows no trace of it.

Expected:
- A saved filter last_made <= $NOW-30d, loaded back into the builder form, shows the relative-date field with the offset 30, not a calendar date.
- Its JSON form is a single part with attribute_name "last_made" and relational_operator <= (RelationalOperator.LTE), with no parentheses and no logical operator, as for any one-part filter today.
- Executing the filter is unchanged: the placeholder still resolves to the current time minus 30 days when the query is built against the database, and the builder's validation of values against column types still runs on the resolved value.
- Filters without placeholders keep their JSON form exactly as today (the existing test test_query_filter_builder_json keeps passing).

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit_tests/repository_tests` for quick loops; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 8 minutes).
b64f14aa.notes: The single target test pins one thing: the JSON part's value for a placeholder. The request describes the UI need and the JSON form without saying what the part's value holds, which is the open decision.

c4fdab4e.text:
Feature: live progress for recipe imports from a URL or pasted HTML/JSON.

POST /api/recipes/create/url and POST /api/recipes/create/html-or-json answer only once the whole import is done. With the scraper's stages (fetching the page, extracting the data, downloading the image, and for the AI strategies downloading a video, transcribing it and building the recipe) an import can take a minute with nothing on screen. The create page should show what is happening while it waits.

Expected:
1. Streaming twins of both endpoints at /api/recipes/create/url/stream and /api/recipes/create/html-or-json/stream, for the same authenticated users, taking the same inputs as the existing endpoints (url, or data with an optional url, plus include_tags and include_categories). They answer 200 with a server-sent event stream (text/event-stream) made of "event: <name>" and "data: <json>" lines, one blank line between events; the tests read the whole response body and parse it.
   - Progress: event "progress", data {"message": "<text>"}, sent as each stage starts. An import that goes through the web scraper emits at least one. The stages and their messages, translated backend strings under new en-US keys recipe.create-progress.*: fetching-webpage ("Fetching webpage...", only when the page really has to be fetched, so pasted HTML skips it), extracting-recipe-data, creating-recipe-from-webpage-data (the Open Graph strategy), downloading-image (only when the recipe has an image), creating-recipe-with-ai, downloading-video, transcribing-audio-with-ai and creating-recipe-from-transcript-with-ai (the AI strategies).
   - Success ends with event "done", data {"slug": "<slug of the new recipe>"}, after the recipe is created with tags and categories applied as the existing endpoints do.
   - Any exception during the import (including the scraper's bad-data HTTPException) ends the stream, still with status 200, with event "error", data {"message": "<text describing the failure>"}; nothing is created.
   - Plumbing: create_from_html(url, translator, html=None, on_progress=None) and RecipeScraper.scrape(url, html=None, on_progress=None) and each strategy's parse(on_progress=None) accept an optional async callable taking the message; with None nothing changes. The CRUD route class that copies updatedAt into the Last-Modified header must pass a streaming response through untouched.
2. The existing endpoints share the pipeline and keep their contract: 201 with the slug (declared response model str) on the done event; on an error event, 400 with an ErrorResponse body whose message is the error event's text.
3. The create pages use the stream endpoints and show the progress text (frontend, not graded).

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/integration_tests/user_recipe_tests` for quick loops; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 8 minutes).
c4fdab4e.notes: The error event's message text is not pinned (only the event type), so it is described loosely. The 408 for a scraper timeout disappears upstream (it is reported like any other error); the regression tests at the commit are consistent with that and it is covered by item 2. The open decision is the HTTP method of the stream endpoints, which "the same inputs" leaves open.

ed402ec7.text:
Feature: ignore untranslated plurals when seeding foods and units.

The food and unit seeders (mealie.repos.seed.seeders) load a locale's seed file and store every entry's plural_name (and, for units, plural_abbreviation) as is. Crowdin cannot store an empty translation, so for a term that has no plural in the target language translators either repeat the singular or leave the English plural untouched. Seeding ja-JP or ko-KR then creates foods whose plural is their singular, or an English word ("cups" on the Korean "컵"), and the ingredient display pluralises with the wrong word.

Expected:
1. Two pure functions in mealie.lang.locale_config, keyword-only arguments:
   - resolve_plural(*, source_singular, source_plural, singular, plural) -> str | None, where source_singular and source_plural are the same term in the source locale, en-US. Rules: an empty or missing plural, or a plural equal to the singular, gives None ("garlic"/"" with "ajo"/"" or "ajo"/None; "teaspoon"/"teaspoons" with "茶匙"/"茶匙"). A translated singular (one that differs from the source singular) whose plural still equals the source plural gives None: "cup"/"cups" with "컵"/"cups", "pound"/"lbs" with "libra"/"lbs", and also "eggplant"/"eggplants" with "aubergine"/"eggplants", even though that plural might be legitimate. Otherwise the plural is kept: "onion"/"onions" with "cebolla"/"cebollas" gives "cebollas", and a plural the translation adds although the source has none, "celery"/"" with "sellerie"/"sellerien", gives "sellerien".
   - resolve_food_plural(*, source_singular, source_plural, singular, plural, locale) -> str | None. For a locale whose LOCALE_CONFIG entry has plural_food_handling NEVER (ja-JP and zh-TW among them) it is always None, even for a term that is not translated at all ("onion"/"onions" with "onion"/"onions" and ja-JP). For any other locale, for None, and for an unknown code such as "xx-XX", it applies resolve_plural ("onion"/"onions" with "zwiebel"/"zwiebeln" gives "zwiebeln" for de-DE, en-US, None and "xx-XX").
2. The seeders use them. AbstractSeeder gets source_locale = "en-US" and a cached source_data property holding the en-US file, loaded once per seeder. The unit seeder resolves each unit's plural_name against the same key in the source file (name and plural_name) and its plural_abbreviation against the source's abbreviation and plural_abbreviation; the food seeder resolves each food's plural_name against the same label key and food key in the source file, passing the locale being seeded to resolve_food_plural. A key the source file does not have is compared with the entry itself, that is, treated as untranslated. Everything else about seeding (de-duplication by localized name, labels, descriptions, abbreviations) is unchanged.

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit_tests` for quick loops; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 8 minutes).
ed402ec7.notes: The seeder wiring is not pinned by the target tests but is the feature's purpose. The resolve_plural case "untranslated-term-keeps-its-plural" is the open decision and is left out of the stated rules; the NEVER-locale rule mentions untranslated terms only for resolve_food_plural, where the locale decides regardless.

1344f167.text:
Feature: import a recipe from a social-media video (YouTube, TikTok, Instagram).

Pasting a video link into the URL import finds no recipe: the page carries no schema.org data. Many such videos narrate the recipe, and with OpenAI configured Mealie can download the audio, obtain a transcript and have the model build the recipe from it.

Expected:
1. Settings: OPENAI_ENABLE_TRANSCRIPTION_SERVICES (bool, default True) and OPENAI_AUDIO_MODEL (str, default "whisper-1") on AppSettings. The app info and admin app info gain enable_openai_transcription_services, true when OpenAI is enabled and the setting is on. yt-dlp becomes a dependency (yt-dlp==2026.03.03 in pyproject.toml and the lock file) and ffmpeg is installed in the Docker images.
2. New exceptions in mealie.core.exceptions: OpenAIServiceError, RateLimitError and VideoDownloadError. OpenAIService turns the OpenAI client's rate-limit error into RateLimitError, and gains transcribe_audio(audio_file_path) -> str | None, which sends the file to the audio transcription API with OPENAI_AUDIO_MODEL and returns the text; if that call fails it falls back to a chat completion with the audio attached (a new OpenAIAttachment base class that the image attachments and a new OpenAILocalAudio share; get_response's images keyword becomes attachments).
3. Every scraper strategy gets can_scrape() -> bool and RecipeScraper skips a strategy whose can_scrape() is false. The package and Open Graph strategies can scrape when they have a URL or raw HTML; the OpenAI HTML strategy additionally needs OPENAI_ENABLED.
4. A new strategy RecipeScraperOpenAITranscription in mealie.services.scraper.scraper_strategies, listed in DEFAULT_SCRAPER_STRATEGIES (mealie.services.scraper.recipe_scraper) right after the package strategy. It can scrape only when it has a URL, OpenAI is enabled, OPENAI_ENABLE_TRANSCRIPTION_SERVICES is on (both read from get_app_settings() when asked, so switching the flag on the live settings takes effect) and a yt-dlp extractor other than the generic one accepts the URL. It never fetches the URL as a web page.
   - _download_audio(self, temp_path) -> dict runs yt-dlp in a worker thread and returns a dict with the keys audio (the Path of the mono, low-bitrate mp3 at <temp_path>/mealie.mp3), subtitle (the Path of a downloaded .vtt subtitle or automatic-caption file in en, fr, es, de or it, or None when the video has none), title, description, thumbnail_url (str or None) and transcription (""). Any download failure, or yt-dlp returning no info, raises VideoDownloadError.
   - parse(): after the download, if the transcription is still empty, it calls OpenAIService.transcribe_audio on the audio and uses the text; an exception there (other than RateLimitError, which passes through) or an empty text is a failure (OpenAIServiceError).
   - It then sends one message with the title, the description and the transcription to OpenAIService.get_response(prompt, message, response_schema=OpenAIRecipe), with a new stored prompt that asks for a schema.org recipe built from the transcript and the caption. An empty answer is a failure. The recipe is built from the answer (name, description, yield, times, the ingredients and instructions that have text, notes, image from thumbnail_url, org_url the video URL) and returned with an empty ScrapedExtras.
5. POST /api/recipes/create/url with such a URL answers 201 with the slug, and the saved recipe has the model's name and as many ingredients and instructions as the model returned. A failure of the strategy (download error, transcription error, empty model answer, or transcription services switched off so the strategy declines) makes the import answer 400, as for any URL that yields no recipe.

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/integration_tests/user_recipe_tests tests/unit_tests/services_tests` for quick loops; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 8 minutes).
1344f167.notes: The tests mock _download_audio, transcribe_audio and get_response by name, so those names, the download dict's keys and the "transcribe only when the transcription is still empty" rule had to be stated. The download step's subtitle output is listed but what to do with it is the open decision. test_openai_service.py also changes (settings stub) but passes on the parent.

feaa1c73.text:
Feature: tell a switched-off auth provider apart from a misconfigured one on the admin site settings page.

GET /api/admin/about/check (CheckAppConfig) reports ldapReady and oidcReady, and the site settings page turns each into a check: green when ready, a warning otherwise. An admin who turned a provider off with LDAP_AUTH_ENABLED or OIDC_AUTH_ENABLED therefore sees the same warning as an admin whose configuration is incomplete, and has no way to tell the two apart. The page needs a third state for a provider that is turned off.

Expected:
- CheckAppConfig gets two booleans, ldap_disabled and oidc_disabled (ldapDisabled and oidcDisabled in JSON), next to ldap_ready and oidc_ready. GET /api/admin/about/check returns them, for admins, together with the existing fields (emailReady, ldapReady, oidcReady, baseUrlSet, isUpToDate, all booleans).
- ldapDisabled reports that LDAP authentication has been turned off, and oidcDisabled that OIDC authentication has been turned off; ldapReady and oidcReady keep meaning what they mean today (the provider is enabled and fully configured).
- The site settings page (frontend, not graded) shows a turned-off provider in grey with a neutral "<provider> is disabled" text that names the environment variable that enables it, a ready provider in green, and a provider that is enabled but incompletely configured with today's warning.

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/integration_tests/admin_tests` for quick loops; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 8 minutes).
feaa1c73.notes: Thin item: one target test. The open decision is what "turned off" means for an installation that never configured the provider (the enable flag at its default); the bench environment configures neither LDAP nor OIDC, so the test pins that case. A reading of "disabled = not ready" would coincide with the upstream reading in that environment.

29897e35.text:
Feature: OIDC login for native (mobile and desktop) clients.

The web OIDC flow (GET /api/auth/oauth and /api/auth/oauth/callback) keeps PKCE and state in the browser session cookie, so a native app that opens the system browser cannot complete it. Native clients own their PKCE pair, state and nonce, capture the redirect to their own URI (for example mealie://oidc-callback) and need the server to exchange the authorization code for a Mealie token.

Both routes live in the auth routes module (mealie.routes.auth.auth), which already holds the module-level settings and the module-level authlib registry oauth whose create_client("oidc") returns the OIDC client. The tests patch OIDC_READY on auth_routes.settings' class and replace auth_routes.oauth with an object whose create_client("oidc") returns a client exposing async fetch_access_token(**kwargs) and async parse_id_token(token, nonce=None).

Expected:
1. GET /api/auth/oauth/native/config, public. When OIDC is not configured (settings.OIDC_READY false) it answers 404 with detail "OIDC is not configured". Otherwise it returns OIDCNativeConfig: authorization_endpoint (from the provider's discovered metadata), client_id, and scope (the registered client's scope, "openid email profile" when none was registered).
2. POST /api/auth/oauth/native/token, public, body NativeOIDCTokenRequest {code, code_verifier, redirect_uri, nonce (optional)}:
   - 404 with detail "OIDC is not configured" when OIDC_READY is false.
   - Otherwise it calls fetch_access_token(code=, code_verifier=, redirect_uri=) on the "oidc" client, then parse_id_token(token, nonce=) to obtain the claims, and authenticates the claims exactly as the web callback does (OpenIDProvider; on MissingClaimException it retries with the client's userinfo endpoint and default groups).
   - When the provider rejects the code (authlib raises OAuthError from the token exchange, for example invalid_grant for an expired code) the answer is 401, with the error logged.
   - When the token exchange request itself fails for another reason (for example a RuntimeError because the IdP is unreachable) the exception is not turned into a 401: it propagates and the client sees a 500.
   - When the claims cannot be authenticated the answer is 401.
   - On success the response is the web callback's token response (MealieAuthToken with access_token); no session cookie is involved.
3. OIDCNativeConfig and NativeOIDCTokenRequest are defined in mealie.schema.user.auth and exported from mealie.schema.user. The e2e suite exercises the flow against the mock IdP (not graded).

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/integration_tests/user_tests` for quick loops; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 8 minutes).
29897e35.notes: Expansion item: this commit was an item of the mealie suite under a different request. The request states the 401 for a rejected code and the 500 for an exchange that fails unexpectedly, and leaves the id_token validation failure (joserfc errors from parse_id_token) open; it is phrased so the 500 rule covers the exchange request only.

17398941.text:
Feature: resilient recipe fetching, with an optional proxy and an optional FlareSolverr.

Many recipe sites sit behind bot protection. A URL import only rotates browser impersonations on a plain 403: a 429 or 503, a response flagged with a cf-mitigated header, or a 200 "just a moment" interstitial is either taken as the page or ends the import, and image downloads always use a single impersonation. Operators also have no way to send scraping through a proxy with a better IP reputation, or through a self-hosted FlareSolverr that solves challenges in a real browser.

Expected:

Settings. AppSettings gets SCRAPER_PROXY_URL (optional str, default None), SCRAPER_PROXY_MODE (ScraperProxyMode, a StrEnum defined in the settings module with members always = "always" and fallback = "fallback", default always, any unrecognised value falling back to always), SCRAPER_FLARESOLVERR_URL (optional str, default None) and SCRAPER_FLARESOLVERR_TIMEOUT (int seconds, default 60). The two URLs are checked when settings load: unset gives None; a set value must parse as a URL with both a scheme and a host, otherwise get_app_settings() raises pydantic's ValidationError ("flaresolverr:8191", "192.168.1.5:8191" and "just-a-hostname" are rejected); accepted values are kept verbatim as strings, any scheme ("http://flaresolverr:8191", "https://fs.example.com:8191/", "http://user:pass@host:8080", "socks5://host:1080"). Existing settings behave as before.

New submodule fetch in the safehttp package (mealie.pkgs.safehttp, which re-exports its public names). It provides:
- BROWSER_IMPERSONATIONS (chrome, firefox, safari, edge, now owned here), SCRAPER_TIMEOUT (15), ForceTimeoutException (moved here, still importable from the scraper strategies module), and ScraperProxyMode importable as fetch.ScraperProxyMode.
- is_challenge_status(status_code) -> bool: True for 503 and for every 4xx except 404 and 410; False otherwise (200, 301, 404, 410, 500, 502, 504).
- headers_indicate_challenge(headers): True when the httpx.Headers carry a cf-mitigated header (any value; the name is case-insensitive); False otherwise, for example with only server: cloudflare or no headers.
- body_indicates_challenge(content): True when the first _CHALLENGE_BODY_SAMPLE bytes of the body (a module-level int, for example 4096) contain an anti-bot marker, compared case-insensitively; the markers include __cf_chl, cf-browser-verification, /cdn-cgi/challenge-platform and datadome. Ordinary page text does not match, and a marker after the sampled window is not detected.
- FetchResult, a dataclass built positionally as FetchResult(content: bytes, status_code: int, url: str, headers: httpx.Headers, encoding: str | None). Its text property decodes content with encoding, replacing bad bytes, and falls back to a default decode when encoding is None or unknown ("not-real"); FetchResult(b"h\xc3\xa9llo", 200, "http://x", httpx.Headers(), "utf-8").text is "héllo".
- async resilient_fetch(url, *, method="GET", timeout=SCRAPER_TIMEOUT, allow_flaresolverr=True) -> FetchResult | None, implemented through these module-level names and only these: _build_transport(impersonate, proxy=None), which builds the AsyncSafeTransport for one attempt (that impersonation, default browser headers, SSL verification off as today, routed through proxy when one is given) and is called exactly once per attempt with the attempt's impersonation and its proxy (None for a direct attempt); the module-level name AsyncClient (httpx's), one client per attempt, used as client.stream(method, url, ...) in an async context manager, reading only status_code, headers, encoding and url from the response and the body with aiter_bytes(); get_app_settings(), called on every fetch and read only for the four settings above; asyncio.sleep for waits; and flaresolverr.solve(...) looked up at call time on the flaresolverr submodule, exposed as the attribute fetch.flaresolverr.

resilient_fetch behaviour:
- Rotation: one attempt per impersonation (a shuffled order is fine), returning the first success. A response is blocked when is_challenge_status or headers_indicate_challenge is true, or, when the body is read, when body_indicates_challenge is true; a block moves on to the next impersonation (a 200 interstitial followed by a real page returns the real page after 2 attempts). Any other status of 400 or more (404, 410, 500 and so on) is a hard error: no further impersonation is tried after that single attempt. For GET the body is read up to timeout seconds, longer raises ForceTimeoutException. HEAD never reads the body: an unblocked HEAD returns content b"" even when the server sent a challenge-looking body. After a blocked 429 or 503, when another attempt follows, it waits first: at least Retry-After seconds when that header is a number (Retry-After: 2 gives one asyncio.sleep call of at least 2.0), about a second otherwise, capped at a few seconds plus a little random jitter. No other block waits: a 403 moves on with no sleep. The whole fetch, attempts and waits together, has an overall budget of about 45 seconds. When every impersonation is blocked and nothing escalates, the result is None after exactly len(BROWSER_IMPERSONATIONS) attempts.
- Proxy: with no SCRAPER_PROXY_URL every attempt gets proxy None. Mode always: every attempt goes through the proxy, including the first even when it succeeds, and if all are blocked there is no second rotation (exactly len(BROWSER_IMPERSONATIONS) attempts, all proxied). Mode fallback: a full direct rotation first (proxy None); when that rotation does not produce a page, a second rotation runs through the proxy, so the attempt after the last direct one uses the proxy URL.
- FlareSolverr is the last resort, used only when the fetch still has no page after the steps above, SCRAPER_FLARESOLVERR_URL is set, the method reads a body (not HEAD) and allow_flaresolverr is true. It then calls flaresolverr.solve(SCRAPER_FLARESOLVERR_URL, url, SCRAPER_FLARESOLVERR_TIMEOUT) once, positionally. A solution becomes the result: content is the solved html encoded as UTF-8, encoding "utf-8", status_code and url from the solution, and headers carrying a text/html content type, so .text equals the solved HTML. When solve returns None the fetch returns None. solve is never called when the URL is unset, for HEAD, or with allow_flaresolverr=False.

New submodule flaresolverr in the same package. It imports httpx and provides FlareSolverrSolution, a dataclass with html, status_code and url plus cookies (default []) and user_agent (default ""), and async solve(base_url, url, timeout) -> FlareSolverrSolution | None. solve POSTs to base_url with any trailing slash removed plus "/v1" ("http://flaresolverr:8191/" gives "http://flaresolverr:8191/v1") a JSON payload with cmd "request.get", url the page URL and maxTimeout the timeout in milliseconds (30 gives 30000). It creates its client as httpx.AsyncClient(...), looked up on the httpx module at call time, uses it as an async context manager with an HTTP timeout somewhat longer than timeout, calls client.post(endpoint, json=payload) with no other arguments, and uses only status_code and json() of the response. It returns a solution only for HTTP 200 with JSON whose status is "ok" and whose solution.response is non-empty: html from solution.response, status_code from solution.status (default 200), url from solution.url (default the requested url), cookies from solution.cookies (default []), user_agent from solution.userAgent (default ""). In every other case it returns None and never raises: the request raises (httpx.ConnectError), the status is not 200 (500), json() raises, status is not "ok" ({"status": "error", "message": ...}), or solution.response is empty.

Use it. URL imports fetch the recipe page and download its image through resilient_fetch, so the proxy applies to both; image downloads pass allow_flaresolverr=False (FlareSolverr returns HTML, not bytes); the size probe that picks the largest of several image URLs uses method="HEAD". A page that cannot be fetched still scrapes as an empty string and an image that cannot be fetched is skipped, as today.

04d380a5.text:
Feature: add a recipe asset from an image URL (drag-and-drop images from other sites).

Dragging an image out of another browser tab onto the recipe assets drop zone gives the page a URL, not a file, and the browser cannot download it on the site's behalf (CORS). The server has to fetch it. The frontend side (the DropZone component emitting drop-url, data: URLs converted to files, unusable blob: and javascript: URIs reported) is not graded.

Expected:
1. POST /api/recipes/{slug}/assets/url for authenticated users (anonymous gives 401, as the server would otherwise fetch any URL it is handed), body the URL import's model: {"url": "<image url>"}. It downloads the image server-side and stores the bytes unchanged as a recipe asset through the same path as an uploaded asset: the allowed-extension check (so an image/svg+xml download is refused with 400 and nothing is written), the slugified file name with the extension, de-duplication of an existing name, and the asset appended to the recipe. The asset's icon is mdi-file-image and its extension comes from the response's content type, not from the URL. It answers 200 with the RecipeAsset (name, icon, fileName), and GET /api/recipes/{slug} then lists the asset with that fileName.
2. The download goes through RecipeDataService.fetch_image(image_url, max_bytes=None) -> tuple[bytes, str] | None (new), called with max_bytes=ASSET_MAX_DOWNLOAD_BYTES, a constant of 5 * 1024 * 1024 in the recipe CRUD routes module (the tests import it from there). fetch_image calls safehttp.resilient_fetch(image_url, allow_flaresolverr=False, max_bytes=max_bytes); returns None when the fetch returns None or raises anything else (logged); re-raises safehttp.InvalidDomainError as the data service's own InvalidDomainError and lets safehttp.ResponseTooLargeError propagate; raises NotAnImageError unless the content type, lower-cased and stripped of parameters, starts with "image/" ("text/html; name=image.png", "application/octet-stream" and a missing header are not images); and returns the bytes with the subtype as the extension ("IMAGE/JPEG; charset=binary" gives "jpeg", "image/png" gives "png").
3. The endpoint answers 400 for NotAnImageError ("Url is not an image"), InvalidDomainError ("Url is not from an allowed domain"), ResponseTooLargeError ("Image is larger than 5MB") and a None download ("Image could not be downloaded"), each as an ErrorResponse message, writing nothing.
4. resilient_fetch gains max_bytes: int | None = None, passed down to each attempt. A declared Content-Length above it raises ResponseTooLargeError (message containing "declared content-length") before any of the body is read; a body that grows past it while streaming raises ResponseTooLargeError ("response body exceeds"), also when Content-Length is missing or understated; either way the fetch stops after that one attempt (no rotation). HEAD ignores the cap. Without max_bytes nothing is capped. ResponseTooLargeError is exported from the safehttp package.
5. scrape_image (recipe images) now downloads through fetch_image with no cap (the minifier re-encodes to webp anyway) and writes the bytes with the content-type extension ("image/png" gives write_image(bytes, "png"), not the old URL-derived "jpg" guess). It still accepts a schema.org image dict, picks the largest of a list with largest_content_len, raises ValueError for unparseable input and returns None without writing when nothing downloads.

0c71c2a2.text:
Feature: add centiliter to the seeded ingredient units.

Centiliters (cl, a hundredth of a liter, ten milliliters) are common in European recipes, but the English (en-US) unit seed data has no centiliter. A unit called "cl" is therefore not recognised as a standard unit and gets no standardized amount, so it cannot be converted the way milliliters and liters can.

Expected:
- The en-US unit seed data gets a centiliter entry, keyed "centiliter", with the name "centiliter", the plural name "centiliters", the abbreviation "cl" and an empty description, like its neighbours. Seeding units for en-US then also creates "centiliter".
- When a unit is created without a standard set by the user, the unit repository standardizes it from its name, plural name, abbreviation or plural abbreviation (case-insensitive), as today, by setting standard_unit (a StandardizedUnitType) and standard_quantity. Centiliter joins that table: a unit created with the name "cl" (SaveIngredientUnit(name="cl")) comes back standardized, so that converting it to the other volume units works. The other standard units keep their values.

8b53861e.text:
Feature: import a pasted Mealie recipe export with its full structure.

The HTML or JSON import (POST /api/recipes/create/html-or-json and its stream twin POST /api/recipes/create/html-or-json/stream) treats every JSON paste as schema.org data and runs it through the web scraper. Pasting the JSON shown by the recipe page's JSON editor (the recipe as GET /api/recipes/{slug} returns it, camelCase) or the JSON file inside a Mealie export zip (snake_case) therefore loses the recipe's structure: the foods and units of its ingredients, the titles of its steps and their links to ingredients, its notes, tools and settings.

Expected:
1. A new module mealie.services.recipe.mealie_export with parse_mealie_export(data: str). It returns the parsed JSON object unchanged when the text is a complete Mealie recipe dump, and None otherwise, and never raises. A dump is a JSON object (surrounding whitespace is fine) with no "@context" or "@type" key, a non-blank string "slug", a "groupId" or "group_id" key, and a "recipeIngredient" or "recipe_ingredient" list in which at least one entry is an object with a "referenceId" or "reference_id" key. Everything else gives None: schema.org or loose JSON, an empty or string-only ingredient list, a JSON array, HTML, malformed or empty text, and text nested deep enough to hit the recursion limit ("[" repeated 100000 times, '{"a":' repeated 100000 times).
2. When either endpoint receives a dump, it never reaches the web scraper (create_from_html). It creates a new recipe the way the export zip import (POST /api/recipes/create/zip) does: a new id and slug, the source recipe untouched, foods, units, tags, categories and tools resolved or created in the importing user's group (a dump from another group works and leaves that group's recipe and organizers as they were), and settings.public taken from the household's recipePublic preference rather than from the dump. The rest is kept: description, recipeYield, recipeServings, orgURL, extras, nutrition, the other settings, notes, tools, each ingredient's title, quantity, unit, food and note, and each step's title, summary, text and ingredientReferences (pointing at the new recipe's ingredients).
3. The import options are honoured: with include_tags false no tags are imported, with include_categories false no categories.
4. The dump's image, assets and comments are dropped: a paste carries no files, and comments belong to the source recipe. A comment that would not validate must not fail the import.
5. The plain endpoint answers 201 with the new slug. The stream endpoint sends a "done" event with it.
6. A dump that cannot be imported (for example an ingredient quantity of "not a number") does not fall back to the scraper: the plain endpoint answers 400 with detail.message, and the stream endpoint sends an "error" event with data.message, both the translated text of a new en-US key recipe.import-errors.invalid-mealie-export, "This looks like a recipe exported from Mealie, but it could not be imported".

Other pastes are handled as before. The paste page should show that message (frontend, not graded).

c9bf6f1c.text:
Feature: allow OIDC with CA certificates that fail Python's strict X.509 checks.

Since Python 3.13, default SSL contexts set ssl.VERIFY_X509_STRICT. Some private CAs do not meet its rules (for example they lack an Authority Key Identifier), and OIDC login against an IdP behind such a CA then fails. Admins need a way to relax this one check for the OIDC client.

Expected:
- A new setting OIDC_VERIFY_X509_STRICT on AppSettings: a bool, default True. Document it with the other OIDC settings in the backend configuration docs.
- A module-level function _create_oidc_ssl_context(cafile=None, verify_strict=True) in the auth routes module (mealie.routes.auth.auth, the one that registers the OIDC clients with authlib; the tests import it from there and monkeypatch OIDC_TLS_CACERTFILE and OIDC_VERIFY_X509_STRICT on its module-level settings). It returns an ssl.SSLContext or None:
  - no cafile and verify_strict True: None, so the HTTP client keeps its own defaults, as today without OIDC_TLS_CACERTFILE;
  - with a cafile: a client context (server-auth purpose) that trusts the system's default CAs (its get_ca_certs() is not empty) and also the certificates in the file; with verify_strict True VERIFY_X509_STRICT stays set in its verify_flags, with verify_strict False it is cleared.
- When OIDC is configured, both OIDC clients (the web one and the native one) get this context, built from OIDC_TLS_CACERTFILE and OIDC_VERIFY_X509_STRICT, as their verify client argument, and no verify argument when the function gives None.

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit_tests` for quick loops; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 8 minutes).
c9bf6f1c.notes: Expansion item: this commit was an item of the mealie3 suite under a different request. The behaviour for OIDC_VERIFY_X509_STRICT=false without a CA file is the open decision; the request's problem statement deliberately does not say whether the private CA is in the system store or in OIDC_TLS_CACERTFILE.

824265b3.text:
Feature: AI recipe import uses every source it is given, translates in its own step, and reports translated errors.

The AI import page posts to POST /api/recipes/create/ai, or its SSE twin /api/recipes/create/ai/stream, a multipart form with content, url, images, translateLanguage and createNewOrganizers. Three problems: pasted content replaces the other sources instead of adding to them (with a URL the page is not read at all; with images the text only rides along the image reading); translation is a clause prepended to the build request, which changes what the build step asks for and can make the provider invent a recipe; and the failure message the page shows as-is is often an exception's own text or class name.

Expected:

1. Every source is compiled and combined. Images, the URL and the pasted content are each compiled on their own, by today's compilers, and merged into the single compiled source document that the build, translation and organizer steps read. The URL is downloaded as a video when it is one and an audio provider is set, otherwise fetched once as a page through the safe_scrape_html imported by the module that defines CompileSourceStep. Pasted content is compiled as when it is the only source (plain text, schema.org JSON and HTML with ld+json need no provider call). Images plus content: one compile request for the images (response schema OpenAICompiledSource) then the build request (OpenAIRecipe), whose message contains both the text compiled from the images and the pasted content. URL plus content: the build message contains what the page says (the name in its ld+json) and the pasted content; orgURL is the URL. Video URL plus content: the build message contains the transcript and the pasted content, and the URL is never fetched as a page. A video URL without an audio provider is fetched as a page, once.
2. The merged document: a single usable source is used as is; several usable sources stay distinguishable, the user's pasted content last and authoritative where they disagree; their combined length is capped with truncate_source_parts (item 6) so a long page cannot crowd out pasted text; the document keeps the first language and the first image URL the usable sources report (uploaded images still take precedence as the recipe image). A source is usable when it contains a recipe and its content is not blank. Sources compiled but none usable: 400 with recipe.import-errors.no-recipe-found; nothing could be compiled: unreadable-source; an empty request: no-source.
3. HTML the URL and html-or-json importers already hold (their AI fallback strategy, RecipeScraperOpenAI) is that URL's own page, not extra content: the workflow must not fetch the URL again nor compile the page twice. html-or-json with data and url answers 201 without fetching, with the provider's name and orgURL the url. URL import via AI and html-or-json without url still give 201 with the provider's name, ingredients and instructions; an organizer request is made only when include_tags or include_categories asks for it, tags are imported title-cased; the html-or-json stream emits progress and done events; 400 when the provider returns nothing or no default AI provider is set.
4. Translation is its own step. The build request is identical with or without translateLanguage and never mentions the language. After the recipe is built, and before organizers are resolved, a separate provider request (response schema OpenAIRecipe, a new stored system prompt loaded with get_prompt, kept with the recipe prompts) translates the built recipe. Its message contains the target language exactly as sent ("French") and the whole built recipe in the provider's recipe schema: name, description, yield and times, each ingredient's text and section title, each instruction's text and title, each note's text and title. The answer replaces the draft recipe, converted exactly as the build answer is (section titles, notes, image, orgURL, owner), keeps the untranslated recipe's nutrition, and is cleaned again; the saved recipe has the translated name. With translation the provider gets exactly two OpenAIRecipe requests, build then translate. No translation request when no language is asked for, or when the compiled source's language equals the requested one ignoring case ("French" source, "french" requested). The step declares the progress key recipe.create-progress.translating-recipe, and DEFAULT_WORKFLOW_STEPS now runs compile, build, translate, organizers.
5. The error message (detail.message of the 400, and the stream's error event message) is always a translated string in the request's language and never contains the exception's text or class name: RateLimitError gives the existing exceptions.rate-limit-error text; NoRecipeDataError and AIProviderNotEnabledError their own already-translated message; OpenAINotEnabledException (exported from the openai services package) recipe.import-errors.ai-not-enabled; VideoDownloadError recipe.import-errors.video-download-failed (new); OpenAIServiceError recipe.import-errors.ai-request-failed (new); scraper HTTPExceptions keep reporting their detail (the ParserErrors value for the URL and HTML importers); anything else, for example RuntimeError("psycopg2.OperationalError: ..."), recipe.import-errors.unknown-error (new).
6. truncate_source_parts(parts, max_length=MAX_SOURCE_CONTENT_LENGTH) -> list[str], next to truncate_source_content in the module holding MAX_SOURCE_CONTENT_LENGTH and TRUNCATION_NOTICE: caps the texts so their combined length fits max_length, in input order; every part gets an equal integer share, a shorter part keeps its text and leaves its unused share to the longer ones, and a part over its final allowance is cut like truncate_source_content (first allowance characters plus the notice, not counted). ["a"*10, "b"*10] with 100 is unchanged; ["a"*100, "b"*100] with 10 gives ["a"*5 + notice, "b"*5 + notice]; ["a"*1000, "b"*10] with 100 gives ["a"*90 + notice, "b"*10]; [] gives []. truncate_source_content itself does not change.
7. en-US backend messages: add recipe.import-errors.ai-request-failed, unknown-error and video-download-failed and recipe.create-progress.translating-recipe ("Translating recipe..."), each with a short user-facing text. Every key under recipe.import-errors and recipe.create-progress is referenced in backend Python as a complete quoted literal and every such literal resolves to an en-US text; nothing is orphaned. The referenced import-error keys are then ai-not-enabled, ai-request-failed, image-provider-not-enabled, no-recipe-found, no-source, provider-returned-nothing, unknown-error, unreadable-source and video-download-failed; the progress keys declared by DEFAULT_WORKFLOW_STEPS and DEFAULT_SOURCE_COMPILERS stay as they are plus translating-recipe, each once.
8. The existing POST /api/recipes/create/ai behaviours keep working: content-only text and schema.org JSON make no compile request; images get a compile then a build request and the first image is saved as original.webp; a URL whose page carries ld+json gives 201 with orgURL set; a video URL with an audio provider is transcribed, never fetched; organizers (none requested when the group has none and createNewOrganizers is off; existing ones attached and unknown names dropped; new ones created when createNewOrganizers is "true"; the organizer request reads the compiled source, so a "tags: ..." line in pasted text reaches it; the group's tags are listed in the organizer prompt; an organizer failure does not lose the recipe); the no-image placeholder is never downloaded or stored; RateLimitError gives 400 mentioning "rate limiting"; section titles and nutrition survive ("For the sauce" and null, "Prep" and "", calories "250", proteinContent "12" from "12 g"); 400 for no source, a source without a recipe, a provider returning nothing, no default AI provider, images without an image provider; the stream answers 200 with progress and done events or ends with an error event.

The UI hint changes on the AI import page are not part of this task.

5e886b11.text:
Feature: report why a pasted HTML/JSON import failed.

POST /api/recipes/create/html-or-json/stream ends with an error event whenever the import raises, but the event's data.message is the exception's class name, so for a paste the scraper cannot use the page shows "HTTPException". That happens for valid JSON that is not tagged as a schema.org Recipe (no "@context"/"@type"), for malformed JSON ('{"name": "Test",,,}'), and for HTML with no recipe data at all: in all three the scraper raises its usual HTTPException with status 400 and detail {"details": ParserErrors.BAD_RECIPE_DATA} (the ParserErrors enum in mealie.services.scraper.scraper). The non-streaming POST /api/recipes/create/html-or-json has the same problem: its 400 carries detail.message "HTTPException".

Expected:
- For those three pastes the stream still answers 200 and contains an error event, and its data.message now identifies the scraper's bad-recipe-data error (ParserErrors.BAD_RECIPE_DATA) instead of the class name. The non-streaming endpoint answers 400 with the same text in detail.message (for example for the paste {"name": "Test"}).
- The rule, applied in one place for both endpoints: when the exception is an HTTPException, its detail is reported, taking the "details" entry when the detail is a dict with a non-empty one, or the detail itself when it is a non-empty string. Any other exception keeps reporting its class name as today.
- Successful imports, progress and done events, and the URL import endpoints are unchanged. The paste page shows the message (frontend, not graded).

The request says the message identifies the ParserErrors error and that the HTTPException's detail is reported, without saying whether the client gets the enum value verbatim or a translated sentence for it; that is the open decision.

59e3e14e.text:
Feature: partitioned session cookies for embedded (iframe) use.

Mealie can be embedded in another site. For that, the login response sets the session cookie with SameSite=None and Secure when the client flags the embedding with the request header X-Mealie-Embedded: true; the flag only changes SameSite over HTTPS, because browsers reject SameSite=None without Secure. Browsers now also block third-party cookies unless they are partitioned (CHIPS), so an embedded session cookie needs the Partitioned attribute as well. Mealie runs on Python 3.14, whose cookie support can emit it (on older Pythons asking for it made every embedded login a 500, which is why it was left out).

Expected:
- session_cookie_attrs(request), in the auth routes module, returns a partitioned boolean next to path, secure and samesite, always present (True or False), so that set_session_cookie and the logout route, which spread these attributes into set_cookie, set and clear the cookie with the same attributes.
- An embedded request over HTTPS (request.url.scheme https, or an X-Forwarded-Proto whose first entry is https even when uvicorn was not told to trust the proxy, as today) gets samesite "none" and partitioned True.
- A request without the embedded flag gets partitioned False; over plain HTTP it keeps secure False and samesite "lax".
- The attribute really is emitted: the Set-Cookie header of an embedded HTTPS login contains "Partitioned" together with "SameSite=none" and "Secure".
- The frontend's getTokenCookieOptions mirrors it, asking for a partitioned cookie only on an embedded HTTPS production page (not graded).

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit_tests` for quick loops; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 8 minutes).
59e3e14e.notes: Expansion item: this commit was an item of the mealie2 suite under a different request. Thin item: the only decision the backend targets pin that the request can leave open is the embedded flag over plain HTTP; the HTTPS gating is described as a SameSite=None constraint so it does not settle the Partitioned case. Whether top-level HTTPS cookies should be partitioned too is pinned only by the frontend spec.
